Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

damn! interjection

annoyance

also blast!, dammit, damn it, drat, what the devil, damn you

classical

Cic. Att. 5.20.1: quī, malum! istī Pindenissītae quī sunt?
Plaut. Amph. 604: Quās, malum, nūgās?

Malum!

set off by commas inside a question

damn it! what the devil (…)?

(vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs et ōrātiōnibus)

Lewis & Short (s.v. malus, end): malum as an interjection of displeasure, “the plague! the deuce!”. Short a (mālum is an apple).

Other words

  • Vae tibi! — curse you! you’ll catch it!

    <span lang="la">vae</span> with the dative · also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 306; Plaut. Cas. 634: Vae tibi. — Immō, vae tibi sit.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • Dī tē perdant! — damn you! (may the gods destroy you)

    subjunctive of wish; old form <span lang="la">perduint</span> · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 1230; Plaut. Mil. 286

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    A curse, not for a child’s ears; malum and vae are milder.

Examples

  • quī, malum! istī Pindenissītae quī sunt? inquiēs; nōmen audīvī numquam.

    “Who the devil are these Pindenissitae?” you’ll say; “I never heard the name.”Cic. Att. 5.20.1

  • Quās, malum, nūgās? satin’ tū sānus es?

    What damned nonsense? are you quite right in the head?Plaut. Amph. 604

  • Vae tibi. — Immō, vae tibi sit.

    Curse you. — No, curse you!Plaut. Cas. 634–634b

  • Dī tē perdant. sequere sīs mē ergō hāc ad forum, ut solvam.

    Damn you. Follow me to the forum, then, and I’ll pay.Plaut. Ps. 1230

See also alas!, oh no!, bah!.
